title: Named departments
prompt: Show each employee's name and their department's name as department, A to Z by employee.
hints: Unmatched employees don't need to appear.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET name = 'Abe' WHERE id = 15;

solutions: SELECT e.name, d.name AS department FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id ORDER BY e.name;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT e.name, d.name AS department FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id ORDER BY e.name;
SELECT e.name, d.name AS department FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id;

title: Quiet users
prompt: Show the username of users with no sessions.
hints: Find what's missing on the other side.
solutions: SELECT u.username FROM users u LEFT JOIN sessions s ON s.user_id = u.id WHERE s.id IS NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT u.username FROM users u JOIN sessions s ON s.user_id = u.id;
SELECT u.username FROM users u WHERE u.referrer_id IS NULL;

title: Student course counts
prompt: Show every student's name and their number of enrolments as enrolments, including 0.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT s.name, COUNT(e.id) AS enrolments FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT s.name, COUNT(*) AS enrolments FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name;
SELECT s.name, COUNT(e.id) AS enrolments FROM students s JOIN enrolments e ON e.student_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.name;

title: Manager names
prompt: Show each employee's name, and manager's name as manager, or No manager when missing.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT e.name, COALESCE(m.name, 'No manager') AS manager FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT e.name, m.name AS manager FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id;
SELECT e.name, COALESCE(m.name, 'No manager') AS manager FROM employees e JOIN employees m ON m.id = e.manager_id;

title: Cost of what sold
prompt: Show each product category and total cost of units sold as total_cost, using cost times quantity.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT p.category, SUM(p.cost * i.quantity) AS total_cost FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY p.category;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(p.cost) AS total_cost FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY p.category;
SELECT p.category, SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS total_cost FROM order_items i JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY p.category;

title: Order counts by status
prompt: Show every customer's name and their number of pending orders as pending, including 0.
hints: Decide where the status filter belongs.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS pending FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS pending FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY c.id, c.name;
SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS pending FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

title: Retakers
prompt: Show each student's name and course title for courses they've enrolled in more than once.
hints: Group by the student and course.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT s.name, c.title FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id GROUP BY s.id, s.name, c.id, c.title HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT s.name, c.title FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id GROUP BY s.id, s.name, c.id, c.title;
SELECT s.name, c.title FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id GROUP BY s.id, s.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

title: Referred activity
prompt: Show each referrer's username as referrer and the total minutes of the users they invited, as minutes, for those with sessions.
solutions: SELECT r.username AS referrer, SUM(s.minutes) AS minutes FROM users u JOIN users r ON r.id = u.referrer_id JOIN sessions s ON s.user_id = u.id GROUP BY r.id, r.username;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT r.username AS referrer, SUM(s.minutes) AS minutes FROM users u JOIN users r ON r.id = u.referrer_id JOIN sessions s ON s.user_id = r.id GROUP BY r.id, r.username;
SELECT r.username AS referrer, COUNT(*) AS minutes FROM users u JOIN users r ON r.id = u.referrer_id JOIN sessions s ON s.user_id = u.id GROUP BY r.id, r.username;

title: Real order totals
prompt: Show each customer_id and the number of different products they've bought, as products.
hints: A product can repeat across orders.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.product_id) AS products FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(i.product_id) AS products FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id;
SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS products FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id;

title: Temperature jumps
prompt: Show each city and date where the temperature rose by at least 3 degrees from the day before, with the rise as rise.
hints: Self join on city and the previous date.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: UPDATE readings SET temp_c = 5 WHERE id = 2;

solutions: SELECT t.city, t.reading_date, t.temp_c - y.temp_c AS rise FROM readings t JOIN readings y ON y.city = t.city AND y.reading_date = date(t.reading_date, '-1 day') WHERE t.temp_c - y.temp_c >= 3;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT t.city, t.reading_date, t.temp_c - y.temp_c AS rise FROM readings t JOIN readings y ON y.city = t.city AND y.reading_date = date(t.reading_date, '-1 day') WHERE t.temp_c - y.temp_c > 3;
SELECT t.city, t.reading_date, t.temp_c - y.temp_c AS rise FROM readings t JOIN readings y ON y.reading_date = date(t.reading_date, '-1 day') WHERE t.temp_c - y.temp_c >= 3;

title: Missing combinations
prompt: For every category and customer city, show category, city, and how many products of that category were bought by that city's customers, as bought, including 0.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT k.category, t.city, COUNT(b.product_id) AS bought FROM (SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products) k CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT city FROM customers) t LEFT JOIN (SELECT p.category, c.city, i.product_id FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id) b ON b.category = k.category AND b.city = t.city GROUP BY k.category, t.city;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT p.category, c.city, COUNT(*) AS bought FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY p.category, c.city;

SELECT k.category, t.city, COUNT(*) AS bought FROM (SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products) k CROSS JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT city FROM customers) t LEFT JOIN (SELECT p.category, c.city, i.product_id FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON o.id = i.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id) b ON b.category = k.category AND b.city = t.city GROUP BY k.category, t.city;

SELECT c.name, COALESCE(SUM(o.amount), 0) AS spend FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

title: Departments without bonuses
prompt: Show the name of departments where no employee has a bonus above 0, including empty departments.
hints: Filter in ON, then test for NULL.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT d.name FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.department_id = d.id AND e.bonus > 0 WHERE e.id IS NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT d.name FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.department_id = d.id WHERE e.bonus IS NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT d.name FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.department_id = d.id WHERE e.id IS NULL;

title: Users on two devices
prompt: Show the username of users who used more than one device.
solutions: SELECT u.username FROM users u JOIN sessions s ON s.user_id = u.id GROUP BY u.id, u.username HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.device) > 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT u.username FROM users u JOIN sessions s ON s.user_id = u.id GROUP BY u.id, u.username HAVING COUNT(s.device) > 1;
SELECT u.username FROM users u JOIN sessions s ON s.user_id = u.id GROUP BY u.id, u.username;

title: Average spend per city
prompt: Show each customer city and its average line value as avg_line (price times quantity), rounded to 2 decimals, highest first.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT c.city, ROUND(AVG(p.price * i.quantity), 2) AS avg_line FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY avg_line DESC;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT c.city, ROUND(AVG(p.price), 2) AS avg_line FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY avg_line DESC;

SELECT c.city, ROUND(AVG(p.price * i.quantity), 2) AS avg_line FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY avg_line;
